transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess I came in because I’ve been feeling like I’m messing things up for people. Like I’m kind of a fake in my apprenticeship, and when I make mistakes, I feel like I’ve let my family down and the younger apprentices too. I know other people probably just fix it and move on, so maybe I’m making too much of it, but… it’s been hard to shake.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different parts of your life, not just your apprenticeship?

I mean… I don’t think it’s everything, no. Mostly it’s the apprenticeship stuff and, like, not wanting to disappoint people. I guess I worry about my family some too, but I don’t know if it’s more than normal. Does that make sense?
Did these feelings start after something specific happened in your apprenticeship?

Yeah… I think it kind of started after I added the sustainable plumbing certification on top of my apprenticeship. It’s not like one huge thing happened, I guess, but since then—maybe about five months now—I’ve just felt more like I’m not keeping up or I’m letting people down. Does that sound like what you mean?
Have you been feeling down or depressed a lot lately?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed, exactly… I mean, I’ve been feeling pretty low on myself, I guess. But it’s mostly when I think about messing up or not being good enough. I’m still getting through things. Is that what you mean by down?
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… a little, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but lately I’ll walk past my sketchbook and just not even pick it up, or I’ll skip volleyball, and I’ve been ignoring the volunteer group texts. Those used to be things I actually looked forward to… like they made me feel like me. Now it’s more like I just don’t feel much about them. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
For the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling this low most of the day nearly every day?

Most of the day… I guess, yeah, more than I wanted to admit. It’s been kind of hanging around for a lot longer than just a couple weeks—maybe about nine months? I was managing okay enough that I could sort of hide it, but once school and work started slipping, it got harder to pretend it wasn’t there. Does that answer it right?
Lately, have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy?

I’m not totally sure… I mean, I get tired sometimes, but I haven’t really been keeping track of whether it’s more than normal. It’s not something I’ve noticed as a big thing, I guess. Should I be paying more attention to that?
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

I don’t know… maybe a little, but I haven’t really noticed it as a major thing. Like, if I’m tired or stressed I might drift off, but I don’t want to say I’m having real concentration problems if that’s not accurate. What would count as trouble concentrating?
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Um… not like I have a plan to hurt myself or anything. I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is. But sometimes, like when I’m driving home after class, or when I’m lying awake at night, I do catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just… didn’t wake up tomorrow. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Even when you’re not thinking about your apprenticeship or making mistakes, do you still feel down?

I’m… not really sure. I mean, I have normal off days, I guess, but I haven’t noticed feeling down all the time or for no reason. It’s kind of hard for me to separate out what’s “down” versus just stressed, if that makes sense.
When your apprenticeship is going well or not on your mind, do you still feel down?

I guess… not really? If the apprenticeship stuff is going okay and I’m not actively thinking about it, I don’t usually feel down for no reason. At least, I haven’t noticed that. I don’t know if that’s the answer you’re looking for, but it feels more tied to stress than just being sad all the time.
Have these feelings been interfering with how you function at work or school?

A little, yeah… I mean, I’m still showing up and trying to do what I’m supposed to. But my instructors and my foreman have had to kind of chase me about unfinished sketches and some jobs taking me longer than they should. I don’t want to make excuses, but it’s starting to scare me because I worked really hard for this apprenticeship and the certification, and I’m worried I’m getting close to messing it up.
Have you been feeling worthless lately?

Kind of… yeah. I don’t know if “worthless” is too strong, but I keep feeling like I’ve ruined things for everybody. Like I’m somehow faking my way through the apprenticeship, and I’ve let my family down, and even the younger apprentices who look to me sometimes. It’s usually over stuff that other people would probably just fix and move on from, so I know it may sound dramatic… but that’s where my head goes.
Have you had a noticeable change in your appetite lately?
Um… I don’t think so? I mean, nothing I’ve really noticed. Some days I eat kind of weird just because of my schedule, but I wouldn’t say my appetite has noticeably changed. Is that what you mean?
Do you feel your reaction to the apprenticeship stress has been stronger than you would normally expect from yourself?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I know the apprenticeship is stressful for everyone, so I don’t want to act like I’m special or anything. But my reaction feels… bigger than it should be. Like instead of just thinking, “Okay, fix the mistake,” I go straight to feeling like I’ve ruined things for everybody, or like I’m a fake and I’ve let my family down, and even the younger apprentices who look to me. I know that probably sounds like a lot over normal work stress, but that’s kind of why I came in.
When the apprenticeship stress isn’t on your mind, do you still feel down for no clear reason?

I’m not totally sure. I think it’s usually tied to the apprenticeship stuff, or at least that’s what I notice first. When I’m distracted or things are going okay, I don’t think I’m just randomly down for no reason… not in a way I’ve really paid attention to. Is that a helpful answer?
In the past couple of weeks, have there been days when you felt down even when nothing had gone wrong with your apprenticeship?

I… don’t think so, not really. If I feel down, I usually can trace it back to something with the apprenticeship, even if it’s just me replaying something in my head. I haven’t really noticed days where everything was fine and I was just down out of nowhere. Does that make sense?
In the last two weeks, have you had days when you felt down even when you were not thinking about your apprenticeship at all?

I don’t think so… I mean, it’s possible I’m missing it, but I haven’t really noticed days where I’m down and the apprenticeship isn’t somewhere in the background. Usually if I sit with it, I can connect it back to that. I’m trying to answer it the right way—I just don’t want to overstate it.
Before the apprenticeship and certification stress started, had you already been feeling down most days for at least two weeks?

I guess… yes, if I’m being honest. It wasn’t as obvious at first, and I kind of tried to keep it together, but I think that down feeling had been around for maybe nine months. It just got harder to hide once school and work started slipping. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During that nine-month period, was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks when you felt down most days even when apprenticeship stress wasn’t bothering you?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, it’s hard for me to separate it perfectly, but that down stretch was kind of there for about nine months. It wasn’t always dramatic or anything, and I was still trying to act normal, but even before the apprenticeship stuff was really bothering me, I think there were at least a couple weeks where I felt down most days. It just became harder to hide once school and work started slipping.

It wasn’t always dramatic or anything, and I was still trying to act normal, but even before the apprenticeship stuff was really bothering me, I think there were at least a couple weeks where I felt down most days. It just became harder to hide once school and work started slipping.

inference.note: Symptoms now support a depressive episode independent of the apprenticeship stress: at least two weeks of low mood even before the stressor, total duration about nine months, anhedonia, worthlessness/guilt, functional impairment, and passive death wishes. This rules against F43.2 as the primary diagnosis.

opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient endorses a depressive episode lasting about 9 months with depressed mood most days for at least 2 weeks, reduced interest in usual activities, feelings of worthlessness/excessive guilt, passive thoughts of death, and functional decline at work/school. Symptom burden meets criteria for a mild depressive episode. Although symptoms are tied in part to apprenticeship stress, the interview ultimately confirmed at least a 2-week period of low mood even before the stressor was prominent, arguing against adjustment disorder as the best final diagnosis. Generalized anxiety disorder is less likely because worry is not pervasive across multiple domains.
